VLAN-001.root_cause: Trunk encapsulation mode mismatch. Switch 1 requires dynamic trunking protocol auto configuration, whereas Switch 2 is in static trunk mode.
VLAN-001.evidence: Switch 1 Operational Mode is trunk, switchport mode on. Switch 2 trunk native vlan mismatch.
VLAN-001.fix_steps:
Switch1# configure terminal
Switch1(config)# interface Gi0/1
Switch1(config-if)# switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch1(config-if)# switchport mode dynamic auto
VLAN-001.alternative_cause: Mismatched Native VLAN IDs 10 and 99 causing traffic leaks.

VLAN-002.root_cause: VLAN 20 is pruned/missing from the allowed VLAN list on Switch 1's trunk interface Gi0/2.
VLAN-002.evidence: Switch1 Gi0/2 allowed VLANs list shows '1,10' which excludes VLAN 20, whereas Switch2 allowed VLAN list shows '1-4094'.
VLAN-002.fix_steps:
Switch1# configure terminal
Switch1(config)# interface Gi0/2
Switch1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20
Switch1(config-if)# end
VLAN-002.alternative_cause: VLAN 20 is not configured/active in the VLAN database of Switch 1.

VLAN-003.root_cause: Switch port Fa0/5 is assigned to the default VLAN 1 instead of the HR VLAN 30.
VLAN-003.evidence: show interface Fa0/5 switchport output shows Operational Access VLAN: 1 (default) and show mac address-table shows VLAN 1 active on interface Fa0/5.
VLAN-003.fix_steps:
Switch1# configure terminal
Switch1(config)# interface Fa0/5
Switch1(config-if)# switchport access vlan 30
Switch1(config-if)# end
VLAN-003.alternative_cause: Host PC is manually configured with the wrong VLAN Tag or static IP, but Switchport assignment is the direct issue.

VLAN-004.root_cause: Trunking encapsulation mismatch (dot1q on Switch 1 vs ISL on Switch 2) prevents trunk negotiation.
VLAN-004.evidence: Switch 1 running config interface Gi0/2 shows 'switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q' and Switch 2 shows 'switchport trunk encapsulation isl'.
VLAN-004.fix_steps:
Switch2# configure terminal
Switch2(config)# interface Gi0/2
Switch2(config-if)# switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch2(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch2(config-if)# end
VLAN-004.alternative_cause: One of the switch ports is configured in dynamic auto/desirable mode which fails to negotiate.

GW-001.root_cause: HSRP active router priority mismatch. Both routers are configured with standby preemption active, causing interface flapping.
GW-001.evidence: R1 standby priority is 110 (preempt active). R2 standby priority is 100.
GW-001.fix_steps:
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface Gi0/0.10
R2(config-subif)# standby 1 priority 120
R2(config-subif)# standby 1 preempt
GW-001.alternative_cause: HSRP group ID mismatch on subinterfaces.

GW-002.root_cause: The subinterface GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is administratively shut down.
GW-002.evidence: R1 show ip interface brief shows 'GigabitEthernet0/0.10' is 'administratively down'.
GW-002.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0.10
R1(config-subif)# no shutdown
R1(config-subif)# end
GW-002.alternative_cause: The physical interface GigabitEthernet0/0 is shut down, but the show outputs indicate only GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is down.

GW-003.root_cause: Host C has a mismatched default gateway (10.1.10.254) configured instead of the actual router interface (10.1.10.1).
GW-003.evidence: HostC ipconfig shows default gateway is 10.1.10.254, but Router 1 interface Gi0/1 is configured with 10.1.10.1.
GW-003.fix_steps:
HostC# (Update local network properties / DHCP static reservation)
Set Default Gateway: 10.1.10.1
GW-003.alternative_cause: Host is configured with static IP in wrong subnet, or Router interface IP was recently changed.

GW-004.root_cause: Proxy ARP is disabled on Router 1's GigabitEthernet0/0 interface.
GW-004.evidence: R1 show ip interface Gi0/0 output shows 'Proxy ARP is disabled'.
GW-004.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R1(config-if)# ip proxy-arp
R1(config-if)# end
GW-004.alternative_cause: Hosts have missing or incorrect default gateways configured, relying on Proxy ARP as a fallback.

DHCP-001.root_cause: Missing DHCP server configuration on Router 1 for local leases.
DHCP-001.evidence: R1 show running-config has no DHCP pool configuration matching the 192.168.30.0/24 subnet.
DHCP-001.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool LocalPool
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.30.0 255.255.255.0
R1(config-dhcp)# default-router 192.168.30.1
DHCP-001.alternative_cause: Missing DHCP relay agent helper-address pointing to 10.100.1.50.

DHCP-002.root_cause: DHCP address pool utilization is at 100% (pool exhaustion). No IP addresses left to allocate.
DHCP-002.evidence: R1 show ip dhcp pool output lists 'Utilization mark (high/low): 100 / 0' and 'Active bindings: 57' on a pool of max size 62 with 5 excluded IPs.
DHCP-002.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool Finance
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.40.0 255.255.255.128
# (Expands pool size from /26 to /25 for more host allocations)
R1(config-dhcp)# end
DHCP-002.alternative_cause: DHCP lease time is set too long, preventing recycling of inactive IP addresses.

DHCP-003.root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch in DHCP pool (configured as 255.255.255.128 /25, but the router subinterface is 255.255.255.0 /24).
DHCP-003.evidence: DHCP pool configuration has network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.128, but Router subinterface Gi0/0.50 is configured with 192.168.50.1 255.255.255.0.
DHCP-003.next_command: show run | section ip dhcp pool
DHCP-003.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool VLAN50
R1(config-dhcp)# no network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.128
R1(config-dhcp)# network 192.168.50.0 255.255.255.0
R1(config-dhcp)# end
DHCP-003.alternative_cause: Router subinterface IP was configured with the wrong mask, and the DHCP pool mask is actually correct.

DHCP-004.root_cause: DHCP server allocation conflict due to missing ip dhcp excluded-address for statically configured servers (192.168.1.10).
DHCP-004.evidence: R1 show ip dhcp conflict lists conflict for 192.168.1.10 detected by ping, and running config has no ip dhcp excluded-address defined.
DHCP-004.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.10
R1(config)# end
DHCP-004.alternative_cause: Rogue DHCP server on the local LAN segment or IP spoofing from an end client.

DNS-001.root_cause: The DHCP pool advertises an unreachable/dead DNS server IP address (192.168.10.250).
DNS-001.evidence: HostA ipconfig shows DNS Server is 192.168.10.250, but no interface on the router or network matches IP 192.168.10.250.
DNS-001.next_command: show running-config | section ip dhcp pool
DNS-001.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip dhcp pool Pool1
R1(config-dhcp)# no dns-server 192.168.10.250
R1(config-dhcp)# dns-server 8.8.8.8
R1(config-dhcp)# end
DNS-001.alternative_cause: The local DNS server at 192.168.10.250 is shut down or experiencing hardware/software failure.

DNS-002.root_cause: DNS resolution is globally disabled on the router via the 'no ip domain-lookup' configuration.
DNS-002.evidence: R1 running config shows 'no ip domain-lookup' statement alongside 'ip name-server 8.8.8.8'.
DNS-002.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip domain-lookup
R1(config)# end
DNS-002.alternative_cause: The name-server IP address (8.8.8.8) is blocked or unreachable by routing rules.

DNS-003.root_cause: Stale/incorrect DNS A record mapping for 'intranet.local' on the local DNS server.
DNS-003.evidence: DNS server DNS View shows mapping 'intranet.local -> 10.10.10.99', but the actual server IP is 10.10.10.100.
DNS-003.fix_steps:
DNS_Server# configure terminal
DNS_Server(config)# no ip host intranet.local 10.10.10.99
DNS_Server(config)# ip host intranet.local 10.10.10.100
DNS_Server(config)# end
DNS-003.alternative_cause: IP address conflict on the web server itself, or DNS server cache has not expired.

DNS-004.root_cause: DNS Zone configuration error: The DNS server does not host the local domain zone record.
DNS-004.evidence: HostA nslookup shows 'intranet.corp: Non-existent domain' and local DNS view has no host entry for intranet.corp.
DNS-004.fix_steps:
DNS_Server# configure terminal
DNS_Server(config)# ip host intranet.corp 192.168.1.10
DNS_Server(config)# end
DNS-004.alternative_cause: Forwarder configuration on DNS server is incorrect or external registrar is offline.

RT-001.root_cause: OSPF Dead Interval and Hello Interval timer mismatch on the link Gi0/1.
RT-001.evidence: R1 show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 states hello 10, dead 40. R2 show ip ospf interface Gi0/1 shows dead 40.
RT-001.fix_steps:
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface Gi0/1
R2(config-if)# ip ospf hello-interval 10
R2(config-if)# ip ospf dead-interval 40
RT-001.alternative_cause: OSPF Area mismatch (Area 0 on R1 vs Area 10 on R2).

RT-002.root_cause: Missing static route to the remote HQ network (10.0.0.0/8) on the Branch Router.
RT-002.evidence: BranchRouter 'show ip route static' contains static route to 172.16.1.0/24 but lacks any route entry for 10.0.0.0/8.
RT-002.fix_steps:
BranchRouter# configure terminal
BranchRouter(config)# ip route 10.0.0.0 255.0.0.0 203.0.113.2
BranchRouter(config)# end
RT-002.alternative_cause: Dynamic routing protocol (like OSPF or EIGRP) neighbor down or not advertising the network.

RT-003.root_cause: Interface MTU mismatch (1500 bytes on R1 vs 1450 bytes on R2) prevents OSPF database exchange completion.
RT-003.evidence: R1 show ip interface Gi0/1 lists MTU is 1500, whereas R2 show ip interface Gi0/1 lists MTU is 1450.
RT-003.fix_steps:
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
R2(config-if)# ip mtu 1500
R2(config-if)# end
RT-003.alternative_cause: OSPF database too large for the media, or Layer 2 MTU issue on intermediate switch.

RT-004.root_cause: Routing loop caused by mutually recursive static routes pointing back and forth between R1 and R2.
RT-004.evidence: R1 route for 10.200.1.0/24 is via 192.168.12.2 and R2 route for 10.200.1.0/24 is via 192.168.12.1 in routing table outputs.
RT-004.fix_steps:
R2# configure terminal
R2(config)# no ip route 10.200.1.0 255.255.255.0 192.168.12.1
R2(config)# ip route 10.200.1.0 255.255.255.0 GigabitEthernet0/1
R2(config)# end
RT-004.alternative_cause: BGP route redistribution loop or dynamic routing protocol misconfiguration.

ACL-001.root_cause: The inbound Access Control List BLOCK_WEB is filtering all HTTP/HTTPS web traffic and should be disabled on the interface Gi0/0.
ACL-001.evidence: R1 interface Gi0/0 has ip access-group BLOCK_WEB in. ACCESS-LIST BLOCK_WEB denies port 443.
ACL-001.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip access-group BLOCK_WEB in
ACL-001.alternative_cause: A specific rule denies TCP port 443 while permitting port 80.

ACL-002.root_cause: The implicit deny of the VTY access-class ACL blocks admin connections coming from the management host subnet (192.168.1.50).
ACL-002.evidence: R1 access-lists output lists permit statement only for 10.99.1.0/24. Administrator IP is 192.168.1.50.
ACL-002.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip access-list standard ADMIN_ONLY
R1(config-std-nacl)# 20 permit 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255
R1(config-std-nacl)# end
ACL-002.alternative_cause: VTY password configuration missing or SSH key not generated on the router.

ACL-003.root_cause: ACL direction error: ACL is applied outbound blocking return traffic/packets exiting the router interface to DMZ.
ACL-003.evidence: R1 running config interface Gi0/1 has 'ip access-group DMZ_INBOUND out' on interface Gi0/1 (DMZ LAN interface).
ACL-003.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/1
R1(config-if)# no ip access-group DMZ_INBOUND out
R1(config-if)# exit
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
# (Assuming Gi0/0 is WAN interface facing outside)
R1(config-if)# ip access-group DMZ_INBOUND in
R1(config-if)# end
ACL-003.alternative_cause: Rules inside the DMZ_INBOUND access list are missing proper return traffic permit statements.

ACL-004.root_cause: ACL rule order error: The deny statement for the entire subnet (192.168.10.0/24) precedes the specific permit statement for Host A (192.168.10.50).
ACL-004.evidence: R1 show access-lists FILTER lists: '10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any' and '20 permit ip 192.168.10.50 0.0.0.0 any'.
ACL-004.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip access-list extended FILTER
R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 10
R1(config-ext-nacl)# no 20
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 10 permit ip 192.168.10.50 0.0.0.0 any
R1(config-ext-nacl)# 20 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any
R1(config-ext-nacl)# end
ACL-004.alternative_cause: Host A has wrong IP configured or route is missing on Core Router.

NAT-001.root_cause: NAT inside/outside interface designations are swapped (Gi0/0 is configured as outside, Serial0/0/0 as inside).
NAT-001.evidence: R1 running config shows interface GigabitEthernet0/0 configured with 'ip nat outside' and interface Serial0/0/0 configured with 'ip nat inside'.
NAT-001.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# interface GigabitEthernet0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip nat outside
R1(config-if)# ip nat inside
R1(config-if)# exit
R1(config)# interface Serial0/0/0
R1(config-if)# no ip nat inside
R1(config-if)# ip nat outside
R1(config-if)# end
NAT-001.alternative_cause: NAT translation table is full or ACL rule for NAT is blocking traffic.

NAT-002.root_cause: NAT Access Control List (ACL 1) is missing from the configuration database on Router 1.
NAT-002.evidence: R1 running config lists 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface GigabitEthernet0/1' but show running-config has no access-list 1.
NAT-002.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# access-list 1 permit any
NAT-002.alternative_cause: Missing overload keyword in the ip nat statement, causing single-IP mapping exhaustion.

NAT-003.root_cause: The NAT access control list (NAT_ACL) does not permit/include the Marketing department subnet (192.168.20.0/24).
NAT-003.evidence: R1 show access-lists NAT_ACL shows rule: '10 permit 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255' but no statement for 192.168.20.0/24.
NAT-003.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# ip access-list standard NAT_ACL
R1(config-std-nacl)# 20 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255
R1(config-std-nacl)# end
NAT-003.alternative_cause: Route to the Marketing LAN interface is missing on the Border Router.

NAT-004.root_cause: Static NAT configuration error: Mismatched host IP (mapped 192.168.1.100 instead of server's actual IP 192.168.1.10).
NAT-004.evidence: R1 running config shows static NAT mapping: 'ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.10', but show ip interface brief indicates server IP is 192.168.1.10.
NAT-004.fix_steps:
R1# configure terminal
R1(config)# no ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.10
R1(config)# ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.10 203.0.113.10
R1(config)# end
NAT-004.alternative_cause: DNS record maps the public server domain to the wrong public IP address.

WLAN-001.root_cause: WPA2 Pre-Shared Key (PSK) password mismatch on client configuration.
WLAN-001.evidence: AP show dot11 ssid Office-WiFi lists Pre-Shared Key: CompPass123!, but Host_Device profile shows Pre-Shared Key: CompPass123.
WLAN-001.fix_steps: Host_Device# configure wireless profile 'Office-WiFi' security wpa2-psk key CompPass123!
WLAN-001.alternative_cause: DHCP allocation failure on the AP wireless VLAN interface.

WLAN-002.root_cause: SSID broadcasting is disabled on the WLC for the Guest-WiFi profile.
WLAN-002.evidence: WLC show wlan 2 output lists: 'Broadcast SSID................................... Disabled'.
WLAN-002.fix_steps:
WLC# configure terminal
WLC(config)# wlan 2
WLC(config-wlan)# broadcast-ssid
WLC(config-wlan)# end
WLAN-002.alternative_cause: The Guest-WiFi SSID profile status is disabled (turned administrative down).

WLAN-003.root_cause: Switch access port Fa0/12 connected to the AP is assigned to VLAN 1 instead of being configured as a trunk port to pass VLAN 80.
WLAN-003.evidence: Switch1 Fa0/12 switchport configuration shows Operational Access VLAN: 1 (default) and Administrative Mode: static access.
WLAN-003.fix_steps:
Switch1# configure terminal
Switch1(config)# interface Fa0/12
Switch1(config-if)# switchport trunk encapsulation dot1q
Switch1(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
Switch1(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vlan 1,10,80
Switch1(config-if)# end
WLAN-003.alternative_cause: Access Point trunk port tagging is disabled, forcing all traffic to fallback to Switch native VLAN.

WLAN-004.root_cause: The gateway SVl interface Vlan80 on the wireless router/switch is down.
WLAN-004.evidence: Wireless_Router show ip interface brief shows Vlan80 status is 'down' and protocol is 'down'.
WLAN-004.fix_steps:
Wireless_Router# configure terminal
Wireless_Router(config)# interface Vlan80
Wireless_Router(config-if)# no shutdown
Wireless_Router(config-if)# end
WLAN-004.alternative_cause: VLAN 80 has no active ports, causing the SVI to remain in a down state automatically.
